newsitem.title: FRANCE: France to sell off Thomson in two parts.
newsitem.headline: France to sell off Thomson in two parts.

text.p: The French government announced on Wednesday it planned to privatise state-owned defence and consumer electronics group Thomson SA in two parts, starting with defence arm Thomson-CSF early next year.
A Finance Ministry statement said Thomson Multimedia (TMM), the consumer electronics arm, would have to implement a recovery plan and be recapitalised before it could be sold off.

"The government ends the current procedure regarding Thomson SA and decides to start, under two separate procedures, the privatisation of Thomson-CSF, then that of Thomson Multimedia, openly and respecting the state's patrimonial interests," the statement said.
"Thomson-CSF will be privatised as soon as possible in the early months of 1997," it said, adding the state will keep a golden share in the company in order to protect France's defence interests.
The announcement followed the government's decision last week to drop plans to sell off Thomson SA in one go to Lagardere group for a symbolic franc.
France's Privatisation Commission had objected to the conditions under which Lagardere planned to spin off Thomson Multimedia to South Korea's Daewoo Electronics.
The suspension of the privatisation was a major embarrassment for Prime Minister Alain Juppe's government and brought demands from the South Korean government for an explanation from Paris.

The Finance Ministry said precise details of the privatisation procedures would be announced in the next few days after the government consults the State Council, an advisory body which is also the country's highest administrative court.
It said the government would define the best conditions to develop employees' shareholding in the privatised companies.
State-owned Thomson SA comprises 58 percent of defence electronics group Thomson-CSF and all of television and video recorder maker Thomson Multimedia.
Shareholders of Thomson SA last Friday rubber-stamped an 11 billion-franc ($2.12 billion) state capital injection.
At the end of last year, Thomson SA had debts of 25.3 billion francs, of which 13.8 bilion were at TMM and 2.3 billion at Thomson-CSF.
